strongest_angle: During the 2021 Meltwater Champions Chess Tour Finals, Teimour Radjabov faced a critical endgame against Hikaru Nakamura where he had only six seconds remaining to choose his move.

key_facts.fact: In a 2021 Meltwater Champions Chess Tour Finals game, Teimour Radjabov had exactly six seconds left on his clock to decide his move against Hikaru Nakamura.
Teimour Radjabov played the move 48 Kd2, which allowed Hikaru Nakamura to respond with 48... Ke5, securing a winning position for Black.
Following the move 49 Kd3 Kd5, Teimour Radjabov was forced to resign the game against Hikaru Nakamura because he was in zugzwang.
In the final standings of the 2021 Meltwater Champions Chess Tour, Hikaru Nakamura earned 28 points while Teimour Radjabov earned 23.5 points.

quotes.text: Six seconds! That’s how long Radjabov had to choose his next move in the diagram below, from an online rapid game in 2021. Plausible options are 1 Kd3, 1 Kd2 and 1 Kc3, but two of these lose by force.
quotes.speaker: Luke McShane
